title: Play the last second of Signal Sprint
summary: Prove a wrong tap, a right tap and a late tap do three different things.
requires: Use the running example below. For a file you can keep, use Save example (.html) and rename the copy index.html in an empty practice folder.
features: Start the clock and try a good tap, a wrong tap and a late tap. Check the score after each.
roles: Test a timeout on a pretend mail-report screen.
Check a time limit with the same steps on two devices.
Prove which taps count in a timed game.
prompt: Write a short test for one miss, two hits and a tap after the deadline in a 15-second signal game. Give a score and clock reading I can check. Use only the rules and results I supply.

steps.title: Start at a known score
steps.text: Open the sample. Find the build label Signal Sprint 1.0. Select Test mode, then press Start. Look for a score of 0 and 15 seconds.
steps.help: If the seconds fall by themselves, select Test mode and press Start.

steps.title: Test a miss and two hits
steps.text: The first target is Lamp. Tap Bell. The score stays 0 and the target stays Lamp. Tap Lamp, then Bell as the target changes. The score should reach 2.
steps.help: A second hit must match the new target. Copy the target and total after each tap to see which action failed.

steps.title: Cross the deadline
steps.text: Press Advance 1 second fourteen times. The display should read 1. Press it once more. Tap an answer after time runs out. Look for the round to end and the score to stay 2.
steps.help: If time ended while you were choosing, start a fresh manual round. Compare the display just before and just after zero.

steps.title: Repeat from a clean start
steps.text: Press Restart. Check the score, the 15-second clock and the answer controls. Ask the AI to compare its prediction with your three observations, or compare the numbers yourself.
steps.help: Use a fresh round for each attempt. A late tap from the finished round must not appear in the new score.

check: A miss changes neither score nor target. Two correct taps give 2 points and switch the target each time.
At zero the answers lock. Restart begins at 0 points and 15 seconds.

title: Save a first checkpoint with Git
summary: Make a local history of one game file and read back the name of the saved version.
requires: Use a computer with Git installed. Download the game from ship lab 1. Make a new stand-alone folder outside any other project, with just index.html in it. Open a terminal in that folder.
features: Save a checkpoint of the game. Check that it contains just the files you meant to save.
roles: Save the first tested version of a fake mail report.
Keep a checkpoint before changing a team template.
Put the single-file game under version control.
prompt: Read this made-up status and explain what is on disk and what is in the next commit: first ?? index.html, then A  index.html. Suggest one read-only check before the commit.

steps.title: Start the local history
steps.text: Run these commands only in the empty practice project containing your game. The status should list index.html with two question marks.
steps.help: If you see separate files or an existing history, stop and open a new separate practice folder. Do not run these commands inside another repository.

steps.title: Use a practice identity
steps.text: Set the two fictional values below for this repository only. Check that the address printed is builder@example.test. Keep this practice history local. For an actual public project, review your approved author identity and GitHub commit email privacy before publishing.
steps.help: The --local setting is for this folder. If Git asks who you are, check these local settings in the same terminal. You do not need to enter personal contact details for this exercise.
steps.code:
git config --local user.name "Practice Builder"
git config --local user.email "builder@example.test"
git config --local --get user.email

steps.title: Choose just the game
steps.text: Stage index.html, then inspect the staged file list. Expect only index.html in the next checkpoint. Open the file itself and look for Signal Sprint 1.0.
steps.help: If a second file appears in the staged list, stop here and use a clean game-only folder.
steps.code:
git add -- index.html
git diff --cached --name-only
git status --short

steps.title: Record and read the checkpoint
steps.text: Commit the game. Write down the short ID printed by git log. Run git status --short. An empty result means there is no remaining change here.
steps.help: If Git says there is nothing to commit, inspect the latest log and file list before trying again. Do not invent an extra edit.
steps.code:
git commit -m "Save tested Signal Sprint 1.0"
git log -1 --oneline
git status --short

check: Only index.html is staged for this first commit.
The latest log shows the game checkpoint. The final short status is empty.

title: Try a release label and roll it back
summary: Make a tiny visible change, inspect it and undo that one commit while keeping the history.
requires: Use the clean local practice repository from ship lab 2. Open a terminal and a plain-text editor in that folder.
features: Change the build label and test it. Then put back the saved version.
roles: Try a report heading before rolling it back.
Check a change to the visible version on a training page.
Restore a known game label and test the restored file.
prompt: Only the visible game build label should change. Explain how I can check the edit before I commit it and how to restore the earlier label while keeping both history entries.

steps.title: Check the starting point
steps.text: Run the two commands. Expect an empty status and the saved game at the tip of the history. Note the short ID.
steps.help: If there is an separate change, use a new copy of the lab before proceeding.

steps.title: Try a visible label edit
steps.text: In the editor, find the visible Signal Sprint 1.0 label in index.html. Change just the text inside the small element to Signal Sprint 1.1 and save. Run the diff and confirm the only intended change is the label. Open the game and look for 1.1.
steps.help: If your editor changed every line or the timer code, do not commit. Return to your saved game copy, edit only the label and inspect the diff again.

steps.title: Save the tiny edit
steps.text: Stage the file and inspect the staged edit. Commit only if it is the label change. Check the log. The newest subject must be Try the 1.1 label.
steps.help: If the staged diff is empty or includes other edits, stop before the commit.
steps.code:
git add -- index.html
git diff --cached -- index.html
git commit -m "Try the 1.1 label"
git log -1 --oneline

steps.title: Reverse just the tested edit
steps.text: Confirm git status --short is empty and that Try the 1.1 label is still the newest commit. Only in that clean scratch project, run the rollback below. Check the three entries. Reopen index.html and look for 1.0.
steps.help: If the newest commit or status differs, inspect the history and stop. This exercise assumes HEAD is exactly the small label edit.
steps.code:
git revert --no-edit HEAD
git log -3 --oneline
git status --short

check: The candidate shows 1.1 with the same game rules.
The rollback creates its own history entry. The restored game shows 1.0 and the final workspace is clean.

title: Catch a pretend secret before shipping
summary: Use a harmless marker to see why both the release file and old versions need review.
requires: Use a second throwaway folder and a copy of the clean game. Keep it separate from your public release and never submit this practice history. Git is needed for the history check.
features: Use a harmless marker to see which files a player can read. Keep private values on the server.
roles: Find a pretend private field in a sample report download.
Review a template and its history before sharing it.
Design a public game with no service key.
prompt: A reader proposes hiding a service key in a comment in a public HTML game. Using only the word PRACTICE_MARKER, explain what a player could read. Say what Git may keep. Name the safe place for a private service call.

steps.title: Plant only a harmless word
steps.text: Make an empty practice folder. Copy the game into it as index.html. Open a terminal in that folder. Run each line. The first line adds a harmless comment to the game.
steps.help: If the folder has any real keys, stop and use a new game-only copy. The marker is just text with no access or value.
steps.code:
echo "<!-- PRACTICE_MARKER -->" >> index.html
git init
git config user.name "Practice Author"
git config user.email "author@example.test"
git add -- index.html
git commit -m "Save game with practice marker"

steps.title: Remove the word from today’s file
steps.text: Delete the comment from this scratch file, save it and commit the removal. Search the current file for PRACTICE_MARKER. You should get zero matches.
steps.help: If the word still appears, check that you opened the same index.html that you edited.
steps.code:
git add -- index.html
git commit -m "Remove the training marker"

steps.title: Check yesterday’s file
steps.text: Run the command. Open the past patch and find the line where the marker was first added and the line where it was removed. Keep this practice repository local.
steps.help: If there is no earlier patch, check that the version with the comment really was committed before you removed it.

steps.title: Sketch the trust boundary
steps.text: Draw browser, your server and outside service. Put a secret only on the server side. Mark where the server checks who is calling and which action they may take. For Signal Sprint, explain why none of this needs to be built.
steps.help: If the AI suggests hiding a key in HTML, look at the marker in the earlier file. For a real exposed key, report it to its owner for revocation or rotation. Never use a live key in this exercise.

check: The current file has no marker. The earlier commit still contains it.
The public game needs no service key. Any later private service call belongs on a protected server with access checks.

title: Serve the same file locally or publish it on Pages
summary: Find out exactly which folder a web server will show. Compare a local rehearsal with an optional public release.
requires: Use a desktop computer, your clean Signal Sprint 1.0 file and Python 3. A GitHub account and the internet are needed only for the optional public path.
features: Serve the folder that holds the finished game. Open the game as a player would.
roles: Rehearse publishing a fictional mail dashboard.
Test a public-safe team schedule without sharing private files.
Publish an independent game copy and check its address.
prompt: I have an index.html file that works on its own and needs no accounts. Name the folder to serve. Give one test that shows the game opened. How can I tell it from a repository page?.

steps.title: Isolate the release file
steps.text: Put only the game in a clean release folder. Run the command below there. Leave the server open.
steps.help: Check that index.html is in the folder you served.

steps.title: Open the local release address
steps.text: Open the local address printed by the server. Read the build label. Start the game and test a tap.
steps.help: If you see a list of files, check the folder and file name.

steps.title: Optional public path · publish the game only
steps.text: For a public test, use a practice repository you may publish. Upload only the approved game file.
steps.help: A public page can be read by anyone. Check the file first.

steps.title: Choose the folder and visit the site
steps.text: In Pages, choose the branch and folder that hold the game. Open the published link and play once more.
steps.help: Use the site link. The code listing is a different page.

check: The local release opens the game from its own folder and shows version 1.0.
For the optional live run, the Pages address opens the game directly. A local-only run is recorded as local only.

title: Retest a release at the address a player will use
summary: Find an old copy by its build label and verify the last playable second on the released copy.
requires: Use the Signal Sprint example below and Python 3 for the local rehearsal. Use a new release-copy folder containing only the saved example renamed index.html. If you published this same safe game in lab 5, you can repeat the checks online.
features: Open the public copy. Check its label, clock and score before you sign off.
roles: Record the tested version of a sample report viewer.
Distinguish a reviewed file from the copy colleagues actually open.
Confirm a timed game still locks after the release is copied.
prompt: Write what you expect and what you see. Give a verdict for each check: visible build, two correct picks, last second, zero, locked answers and restart. Keep the local and public observations on separate lines.

steps.title: Make an old-copy control
steps.text: In a separate folder named old-copy, save a spare game file and change only the visible label to Signal Sprint 0.9. Open it and look for 0.9. Leave the clean release-copy at 1.0. Do not publish the old copy.
steps.help: If both show 0.9, replace release-copy/index.html with the unedited example below.

steps.title: Test the actual address
steps.text: From release-copy, start a local server with the lab 5 command below. In a fresh browser session open http://127.0.0.1:8000/index.html. Record the address, Signal Sprint 1.0 and the short commit ID if you have it. For an optional live test, separately visit the published Pages address in a fresh session.
steps.help: If you see 0.9, check the address, source folder, published branch and last deployment. Reload in a fresh session. Claim only the address where you saw 1.0.

steps.title: Play the boundary case
steps.text: Select Test mode, press Start, then choose Lamp and Bell. Press Advance 1 second fourteen times to leave one second. Press it once more to reach zero. Tap again. Record the score at one second, at zero and after the late tap.
steps.help: If you cannot repeat the timing, return to a fresh test-mode round and read the clock before each action.

steps.title: Sign off or send back
steps.text: Restart and confirm 0 points, 15 seconds and active controls. Stop the local server with Ctrl+C. In your receipt, record any failed check, the exact file or address and the next test. For a bad public release, restore the last reviewed file in the publishing branch, wait for deployment, then repeat these checks.
steps.help: If only the local test ran, mark the public address untested. If a label passed but the lock failed, record both. A correct title does not repair a broken timer.

check: The old control shows 0.9. The tested release shows 1.0.
After two correct picks, the score is 2 at one second and at zero. A late tap cannot add another point.
Restart returns to 0 and 15 seconds. A public pass is recorded only after the public copy is played.
